target_customer: Hospitality employers at first; later AI and software companies needing engineers and AI evaluators
problem: High volume hiring is slow and manual. Hirebolt began by automating screening and matching for hospitality hiring, then aimed its matching engine at engineering talent.
business_model: Recruiting marketplace and staffing: fees for matched talent and AI engineering capacity
product_category: Recruiting and HR tech, AI talent marketplace

founders.name: Alex Zhou
previous_startups: A previous YC company (YC page calls him a 2x YC founder; the company is not named on the page)
founders.background_notes: YC page says he spent three years selling B2B2C tech and attended a top hospitality school, school not named.

founders.name: Lorenzo Sani
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder and CTO in the Index.dev acquisition announcement; the YC page lists only Zhou.

competitors.name: Seasoned
competitors.what: Job platform for the service industry

competitors.name: Snagajob
competitors.traction_then: Large hourly job marketplace by the time of the batch (counts in source are current)

technical_complexity.rationale: Matching, screening and messaging workflows are standard engineering; the hard parts were sourcing and vetting talent.

defensibility.rationale: Many hourly and tech hiring platforms existed and a vetted network is easy to copy.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copying found; Hirebolt was itself acquired by Index.dev, announced March 2026.

market_need_then: Hospitality hiring demand surged after the 2021 reopening and labor shortages made screening costly; no sourced figures opened.

identity.voice_and_tone: Speed focused, with a lightning bolt emoji in its tagline

branding.brand_signature: Speed (bolt) as the promise: results in seconds or days

brand_strength.rationale: A descriptive compound with no press about the brand found; name suited hiring but is shared with other Bolt companies.

pivots.to: AI engineering capacity and talent network
pivots.why: Index.dev says the engine was refined on hospitality hiring and later aimed at software engineering; the YC page now describes AI engineering capacity

outcome_analysis: Hirebolt started in hospitality hiring and later moved to AI engineering talent, with about 1.5 million dollars raised in total per the company and the acquirer. Index.dev announced its acquisition in March 2026 on undisclosed terms. A small team and modest funding, with no later round found, suggest a soft outcome, but the terms and the reason were not public.
notes: YC directory still says Active while the acquisition was announced 2026-03-31 by Index.dev; hirebolt.com remains live. Funding totals conflict: 1.5M (YC page and Index.dev), 100K over 2 rounds (CB Insights), 0.3M (Welcome to the Jungle). The 1.5M is a company stated total, not a dated round. Competitor sources come from aggregator pages and are undated and may postdate the batch. Failure factors are tentative judgments with no stated cause; Index.dev says the deal was strategic. Search summaries mention a possible earlier name ShopScribe and an Imperial College education for Zhou; neither was confirmed from an opened source, so neither is recorded.
